hints: Focus on what each description tells you about position in Period 3, from left side metals to giant covalent to non-metals.
Work out L first. Three unpaired electrons in 3p means a $3p^3$ configuration, so L is phosphorus with atomic number 15.
Now place the best metallic conductor and the highest melting point element on the Na to Ar sequence and compare their atomic numbers with 15.
walkthrough:
**Identify element L from its electron configuration**

Think gently about the 3p sub-shell. It can hold up to 6 electrons, and Hund's rule gives one electron per orbital first.

Three unpaired electrons means $3p^3$, so the full valence is $3s^2 3p^3$. That is phosphorus, P, atomic number 15.

**Identify element M with highest electrical conductivity**

Conductivity in Period 3 is a metallic property. It increases with more delocalised sea of electrons per atom.

$$\text{Na (1 e}^-\text{) < Mg (2 e}^-\text{) < Al (3 e}^-\text{)}$$ 
So the best conductor is aluminium, Al, atomic number 13.

**Identify element N with highest melting point**

Melting point peaks at silicon, not at a metal. Silicon has a giant covalent lattice with strong covalent bonds in all directions that need huge energy to break.

So N is silicon, Si, atomic number 14. This is higher than Al but still lower than P.

**Compare atomic numbers**

We have L = 15, M = 13, N = 14.

Therefore L has a higher atomic number than both M and N.

options.A: Incorrect. It is true that L (15) is higher than M, Al (13), but L is not lower than N. N is Si (14), so L is still higher than N.
options.B: Incorrect. This reverses the order. L, phosphorus, is to the right of both Al and Si in Period 3, so it cannot have a lower atomic number than M.
options.C: Incorrect. This would make L the leftmost element. In fact L is phosphorus, a Group 15 non-metal, which comes after both the best conductor (Al) and the highest melting point element (Si).
options.D: Correct. L is P (15), M is Al (13), N is Si (14). So 15 is greater than both 13 and 14, meaning L has the highest atomic number of the three.
